title: WannierNLQG: A Julia package for nonlinear optical responses and quantum geometry from Wannier tight-binding models
authors: Zhuocheng Lu, Zhichao Guo, Yuanyuan Xua, Jiacheng Yao, Hua Wang
abstract: Nonlinear optical responses and quantum geometry are central to modern condensed matter physics and are deeply intertwined. We introduce WannierNLQG, an extensible Julia framework for computing nonlinear optical responses and quantum geometric quantities from Wannier tight-binding models. Its gauge-consistent, degeneracy-aware architecture accommodates perturbative responses at arbitrary order and additional quantum geometric quantities. The current release evaluates ordinary, spin, and photon-drag injection and shift currents, as Brillouin-zone integrals and on k slices. For shift current, a unified interface exposes four complementary formulations: the conventional method, projector trace, generalized Wilson loop, and a finite-momentum geometric loop, with the last three explicitly accommodating degenerate subspaces. The framework also provides k-resolved Berry curvature, quantum metric, their multipoles, and additional quantum geometric and mixed momentum-spin quantities. Experimental symmetry workflows additionally support symmetry-adapted Wannier construction, symmetrization of tight-binding models and real-space operators, and reduction of spatially uniform response integrals to irreducible k-point orbits and invariant tensor components. The documentation covers formula conventions, the TaskConfig interface, and auditable output formats, with GeS and bilayer MoS2 case studies illustrating method comparison, degeneracy handling, quantum geometric analysis, and photon-drag responses. Together, these capabilities enable first-principles calculations of nonlinear response and quantum geometry in realistic multiband materials, connecting quantum geometry with quantitative materials modeling for optoelectronic, spintronic, and photovoltaic applications.
summary: This paper presents WannierNLQG, a new Julia package designed to compute nonlinear optical responses and quantum geometric quantities from Wannier tight-binding models. It provides a unified, gauge-consistent framework to calculate complex observables like shift and photon-drag currents, while also analyzing geometric properties like Berry curvature. This tool enables first-principles modeling of optoelectronic and spintronic phenomena in advanced materials.
main_problem: The core problem is understanding the deep interplay between nonlinear optical responses and quantum geometric properties in condensed matter systems.
main_result: The authors introduce WannierNLQG, a Julia framework capable of calculating these complex quantities, achieving significant computational speedups over existing methods.
method: The framework uses Wannier tight-binding models to calculate nonlinear currents (injection, shift, photon-drag) and geometric tensors (Berry curvature, quantum metric) via gauge-consistent, degeneracy-aware methods.
model_or_system: The calculations are performed on quantum materials modeled using Wannier tight-binding representations, allowing for extensions to various physical phenomena like moire bilayers and ferroics.
key_observables: Nonlinear optical responses (e.g., shift/injection currents), k-resolved Berry curvature, quantum metric, and higher-order geometric tensors.
important_parameters: Arbitrary orders of perturbation, finite momentum (q), and symmetry group representations.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the validity of Wannier interpolation from first-principles electronic structures and handles degeneracies through specialized formulations (e.g., generalized Wilson loop).
figures_summary: The notes do not provide a detailed figure summary, but mention workflow diagrams illustrating model preparation, response setup, and the final output calculation loop.
paper_structure: The paper details the mathematical formalism for model construction (Wannier gauge, symmetry adaptation), followed by the implementation of various current and geometric tensor calculations, culminating in case studies and performance comparisons.
why_interesting: The focus on nonlinear optical responses and quantum geometry connects directly to advanced topics in quantum optics and the study of open quantum systems, particularly in engineered materials.
